sources.title: Building more with GPT-5.1-Codex-Max
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. November 19, 2025 launch identifies an update to OpenAI's foundational reasoning model, native multi-window compaction and coding-agent training. It gives no nominal total or active parameter count and no counted named base from which to infer size; token efficiency and longer tasks are performance claims.

sources.title: API changelog
sources.evidence: Directly fetched Markdown. December 4, 2025 entry explicitly releases gpt-5.1-codex-max to the Responses API; separates this later milestone from Codex availability.

sources.title: GPT-5.1-Codex-Max API model documentation
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 via official documentation retrieval and freshly fetched Markdown. Exact model is described as a version of GPT-5.1-codex optimized for long-running tasks, with 400,000 context, 128,000 output, text/image input and text output. Documents reasoning, functions, caching and Responses support, but no total/active count. Markdown lists only the undated alias and shut-down status.

sources.title: GPT-5.1-Codex-Max System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full PDF text inspected, including introduction and safety/training sections, and searched for parameter, activated, billion, trillion, architecture and dense. November 18, 2025 cover precedes public release. Describes an updated reasoning base and native compaction without a nominal parameter count, active-count convention or counted base checkpoint.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Directly fetched archived guide explicitly applies to models before GPT-5.6. Explains prompt caching using Transformer attention key/value projections and cached tensors across layers/heads; used with exact Max caching support for a limited operational inference.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Directly fetched guide documents Responses PDF processing for vision models: extracted text and page images enter the model. This establishes an API input format rather than an additional native sensory modality.

sources.title: API deprecations
sources.evidence: Directly fetched April 22, 2026 notice explicitly lists gpt-5.1-codex-max for API shutdown on July 23, 2026. Current model documentation agrees.

sources.title: Addendum to GPT-5.2 System Card: GPT-5.2-Codex
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full PDF inspected. Exact gpt-5.1-codex-max comparisons in Tables 1, 2 and 4 and later capability sections report evaluation results. The document contains no parameter, billion, activated or architecture disclosure that establishes Max total or active size.

sources.title: A Practical Approach to Verifying Code at Scale
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. December 1, 2025 code-review training research explicitly names gpt-5.1-codex-max and says generation/review are tasks of the same underlying model. It supplies no model-size or active-count specification; plot captions refer to GPT-5.1-Codex or GPT-5-Codex and are not size evidence for Max.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Current section 9.1 reserves service intellectual-property rights and grants limited use rights. Supports a descriptive proprietary service classification, not an open-weight license or an assertion about the exact launch-day contract.

sources.title: All OpenAI API models
sources.evidence: Directly fetched catalog lists Max as a retired hosted model, separately from its explicitly identified Apache-2.0 open-weight gpt-oss models.

sources.title: Details about METR's evaluation of OpenAI GPT-5.1-Codex-Max
sources.evidence: Read October 27. Original November 19 evaluation calls Max an incremental improvement over GPT-5-Thinking with no risk-critical architecture changes. Its public developer-assurance table, time horizons and 32M task-token budget do not disclose total/active parameters or establish unchanged numerical size.

sources.title: Claude Opus 4.5 System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh full PDF retrieved October 27. Original model-team comparison Table 2.3.A (printed page 19) lists Codex-Max SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench scores under GPT-5.1. Section 2.5 explicitly identifies GPT-5.1-Codex-Max and notes the Terminal-Bench result was not reproduced by Anthropic. No total or activated parameter column/count is given; these are performance comparisons, not a size convention.

sources.title: IDE-Bench: Evaluating Large Language Models as IDE Agents on Real-World Software Engineering Tasks
sources.evidence: January 28, 2026 original research paper reopened October 27; full PDF text inspected. Exact GPT 5.1 Codex Max appears in Table 1 (task resolution) and Table 3 (average task tokens and efficiency). These are evaluation and token-consumption measurements, not total/active parameter counts. Full-text parameter occurrences refer to tool/API arguments.

name.note: Official exact model name, including its published hyphens.

developer.note: The first-party announcement and model documentation identify OpenAI.

family.note: Generation-specific GPT-5.1 family; Max remains distinct from original Codex and Codex mini.

release_date.note: Earliest explicit public availability is November 19 in Codex. API access followed December 4; the November 18 system-card cover is not a public-release statement. Replaces the original Codex variant date.

open_weights.note: Documented distribution is hosted Codex/API service access. Reviewed primary sources offer no Max weight artifact and separately identify open-weight models.

license.note: Descriptive classification of hosted model access and retained service rights, not an SPDX or downloadable-weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 re-audit found no nominal total in exact documentation, original launch/card, later OpenAI comparisons, training research, METR or original Anthropic/AfterQuery comparisons. The updated-base and version relationships supply no counted base checkpoint. A nominal developer count or explicit counted-base lineage would suffice; the unresolved value is not due to requiring a tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh targeted active/activated-parameter searches and the original research comparisons found no exact-Max active-count convention. Inspected tables report benchmark scores, task tokens or time horizons. Neither compaction, reasoning effort, nor a qualitative architecture-change assessment establishes parameters activated per token.

architecture.note: Qualified operational cross-source inference: exact Max documentation enables prompt_caching and OpenAI's applicable pre-GPT-5.6 guide explains Transformer attention KV caching. This does not establish exclusively Transformer blocks, dimensions, dense/MoE topology or numerical size. Inspected training research does not disclose those details.

context_window.note: Exact documented context window, distinct from 128,000 maximum output. Compaction continues a task across successive windows; millions of cumulative task tokens do not imply a million-token window. No input maximum is derived by subtraction.

modalities.note: Native input is text/image and output is text. PDF records the supported Responses API file format processed into text/page images for vision models; absence of a file_uploads feature flag is not a documented denial. No native audio/video or image output is inferred.

reasoning.note: Exact model supports reasoning tokens; the original release explicitly discusses medium and xhigh reasoning efforts. Compaction and longer tasks are not parameter-count evidence.

tool_call.note: The exact model page explicitly supports function calling in the Responses API; this does not imply availability of every hosted tool.

description.value: GPT-5.1 coding model trained for work across successive context windows, with reasoning, text and image input, and function calling.

patch.notes: GPT-5.1-Codex-Max first became available in Codex on November 19, 2025; Responses API access followed December 4. The system-card cover date, November 18, does not establish public release. The model documentation lists only the undated alias, with no dated immutable snapshot. Its context window is 400,000 tokens and maximum output is 128,000; compaction across successive windows enables longer cumulative tasks without enlarging a single context window. PDF input denotes API conversion into text and page images. Transformer is a qualified inference from exact Max prompt-caching support and the applicable attention-KV mechanism; complete block inventory and dense/MoE routing remain undisclosed. No nominal total or active count is established by the reviewed sources, and the updated reasoning-base relationship supplies no counted base for a size inference. API access shut down on July 23, 2026; these are last-documented capabilities, not a claim of current endpoint operation.

summary: Parameter re-audit October 27: retained undisclosed total and active counts after reopening exact docs, original launch/card, later OpenAI card and code-review research, and checking METR, Anthropic Opus 4.5 and January 2026 IDE-Bench comparisons. No nominal count, counted-base lineage or exact-Max activated-parameter convention was found; performance and task-token figures are not model size. Added explicit null parameter patch values and fresh source evidence. Preserved all 12 other field assessments, including November 19 release, 400K context, qualified Transformer inference and July 23 API shutdown.
